questions.q: How did the swallow make sure the ship could follow her at night?
choices: She sang a loud song so the sailors could hear her
She carried a tiny lantern
She rode on the top of the ship's mast
She flew low, right above the waves
questions.evidence: At night she carried a tiny lantern

questions.q: What did the people on other ships think the swallow's light was?
choices: A lighthouse on a faraway island
The moon shining on the waves
A shooting star
A signal from a pirate ship
questions.evidence: the light must be a shooting star

questions.q: How did the pig, the dog and Too-Too feel about the hot weather?
choices: They could do nothing but sit in the shade drinking lemonade
They loved it and ran about the ship laughing and looking for Africa
They kept cool by jumping into the sea behind the ship
They hid down below in their bunks for the whole voyage
questions.evidence: with their tongues hanging out, drinking lemonade

questions.q: Why did everyone on the boat eat fish on Tuesdays and Fridays?
choices: The flying-fishes brought them a fresh catch on those days
Polynesia said sailors always eat fish twice a week
To make the canned beef last longer
Dab-Dab was only allowed to go swimming on those days
questions.evidence: to make the beef last longer

questions.q: What did the porpoises bring the ship when Polynesia said they were short of something?
choices: Fresh herrings from the sea
Bananas from Africa
Wild onions, in nets of seaweed
Fresh water in large shells
questions.evidence: dragging the onions through the waves in big nets made of seaweed

questions.q: What happened right after the great storm came up near Africa?
choices: The swallow got lost and the ship sailed off the wrong way
The ship struck a rock, got a big hole in the bottom and began to sink
The porpoises pushed the ship safely onto a sandy beach
The anchor broke and the ship drifted far out into the open ocean all night

questions.q: How did Chee-Chee and Gub-Gub get to shore, since they could not swim?
choices: Dab-Dab carried them on her back to the beach, one at a time
They floated to the beach inside the Doctor's trunk
They climbed along a rope that Dab-Dab tied to a palm-tree
The porpoises came back and carried them to land
questions.evidence: those that can't swim must climb along the rope

questions.q: Polynesia calls the rope a "life-line." What is a life-line in this chapter?
choices: A rope that people hold on to so they can get to safety
A line drawn on a map showing the safest way home
A song that sailors sing to keep each other brave in a storm
A long net used to catch fish to eat on a voyage

questions.q: Why did Polynesia have tears in her eyes on the beach?
choices: She was sad the ship was broken
She was afraid of the jungle
She was so pleased to see her own country again
She missed the Doctor's house in Puddleby
questions.evidence: she was so pleased to see her country once again

questions.q: Where did Dab-Dab find the white mouse?
choices: Hiding inside the Doctor's handbag on the beach
Clinging to a piece of wood from the broken ship far out at sea
Sitting inside the Doctor's high hat, floating on the sea
Curled up asleep in the dry cave in the cliffs
questions.evidence: she found one of the white mice, very frightened, sitting inside it

questions.q: Polynesia calls the white mouse a "stowaway." What is a stowaway?
choices: Someone who is very good at swimming in the sea
Someone who hides on a ship to travel without being asked
Someone who is lost and cannot find the way back home
Someone who looks after all the baggage on a long sea voyage

questions.q: Who did the man from the jungle say they must all come before?
choices: The Chief of the Monkeys
The Captain of the ship
The King of the Jolliginki
The Leader of all the Lions
questions.evidence: You must all come before the King
